lead_rationale: The learned PPDDL action effects support held-out workflow prediction, but the study neither executes the induced model as an iterative planner or controller nor frames it as a world model, twin, patient simulator, or reusable dynamic simulator.
full_text_anchor: Primary arXiv Sections 3-5 and Tables 1-3: induced preconditions, probabilistic effects, and next actions are evaluated by held-out prediction and expert review; no planning rollout or closed-loop use is evaluated.

lead_rationale: The action-conditioned latent dynamics are used to construct patient representations for model-free IQL on logged transitions, not as an internal environment for iterative model-based planning, and the authors do not frame the proposed system as a world model or simulator.
full_text_anchor: ACL 2026 Sections 3.1.2 and 3.2.1: the VAE supplies posterior states, while IQL learns from one-step offline tuples and policy value is assessed by FQE; no learned-model rollout is used.

lead_rationale: This is conventional epidemiological network-autoregressive forecasting with posterior predictive calibration, without qualifying world-model, twin, simulator, planning, or closed-loop-control identity.
full_text_anchor: Version-of-record Sections 3 and 5: the fitted Poisson network autoregression predicts next-week county COVID-19 counts and is evaluated by leave-future-out forecasting and randomized-PIT calibration.

lead_rationale: The VAR and transformer models perform ordinary short- and long-horizon patient-reported-outcome forecasting; they are not framed as reusable patient simulators and are not used for model-based planning or control.
full_text_anchor: Version-of-record Methods and Results: weekly radiotherapy outcome sequences are forecast with VAR, VAR-Inc, and TFT and scored by MAE and RMSE against observed trajectories.

lead_rationale: The review surveys single-cell perturbation-response prediction broadly rather than treating learned dynamic world models or reusable biomedical simulators as a central evidence category; much of the covered literature predicts post-perturbation endpoints from static observations.
full_text_anchor: Version-of-record Introduction and objectives O1-O4 organize models by perturbation prediction across omic modalities and discuss temporal response as one challenge, not as a core medical-world-model or dynamic-simulator review.

lead_rationale: BrainLM is explicitly presented as a foundation model and analytic lens for fMRI dynamics, not as a world model or reusable simulator, and its operational dynamics test is ordinary fixed-horizon neural-state forecasting without planning or control.
full_text_anchor: ICLR 2024/bioRxiv Sections 1, 4.3, and 5: fine-tuning predicts the next 20 fMRI time points and evaluates forecast error on UKB and HCP; no iterative simulator, perturbation environment, planning, or closed-loop use is reported.

lead_rationale: The learned rate generator and Neural ODE constitute ordinary epidemiological forecasting, with no explicit qualifying simulator identity and no learned environment used for planning or closed-loop control.
full_text_anchor: Primary arXiv model and evaluation sections: state-dependent epidemic rates advance compartment states for held-out 20-day country and district forecasts against predictive baselines.

lead_rationale: This is conventional population PK and Bayesian therapeutic-drug-monitoring validation; the adapted concentration model is not framed as a twin or reusable patient simulator and is not used as an internal planning environment.
full_text_anchor: Version-of-record Methods and Results: published voriconazole nonlinear mixed-effects models undergo external concentration prediction, Bayesian forecasting, prediction-error analysis, and simulation-based diagnostics.

lead_rationale: The hybrid LSTM-SIRD system is an epidemiological forecasting model, not an explicitly framed world model or reusable biomedical simulator and not an environment for iterative planning or control.
full_text_anchor: Version-of-record model and performance sections: learned time-varying SIRD parameters generate COVID-19 forecasts that are compared with observed epidemic trajectories and forecasting baselines.

lead_rationale: This is conventional population pharmacokinetic model development and validation; multistep concentration-profile simulation does not by itself establish world-model, twin, patient-simulator, planning, or control identity.
full_text_anchor: Version-of-record Methods and Results: NONMEM fits a two-compartment factor-VIII model with covariates and evaluates it through external prediction error and visual predictive checks.

lead_rationale: The fitted symptom-course and morphine-response model is ordinary pharmacometric disease-progression analysis used for regimen simulation, without explicit world-model or patient-simulator framing and without iterative model-based planning or closed-loop control.
full_text_anchor: Version-of-record Methods and test-set Results: a dynamic mixed-effects model with lagged symptom scores and dose response simulates treatment duration and compares predicted with observed duration.

lead_rationale: The neural time-dependent SIR formulation is ordinary epidemiological trajectory modeling, with no qualifying explicit simulator identity and no use as a learned planning or closed-loop-control environment.
full_text_anchor: Version-of-record Methods and Results: five neural networks fit S, I, R, beta, and gamma under SIR constraints and validate reconstructed epidemic trajectories across four countries.
